title: Arkret Device Pairing Short-Link DTOs
description: Closed request and response DTOs for the server-mediated device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md sections 2.1.1 and 2.1.2). Staging is unauthenticated and account-less. Finalize is the one authenticated call that binds a staged record to an exact AccountId by attaching the signed target proof, and it is the only legal one-way step from staged to ready_for_claim. Resolve, the authenticated code claim and status then hand the same byte-equivalent proof and transcript to the approving device; none of them authorizes anything until an accepted device signs ak.device.authorize.

algorithm_list.description: Algorithm ids supported by the target device, sorted by UTF-8 bytewise order and deduplicated before they enter any transcript.

pairing_nonce.description: base64url CSPRNG nonce carrying at least 128 bits of entropy.

gate_audience_uri.description: Origin of the Account Authority gate surface (gate_account_base_url) this pairing request is bound to. Minted by the staging service; the target proof commits to it so a proof cannot be replayed against another Account Authority.

account_id.description: Complete AccountId of the account this pairing request was finalized against. It is a signed member of device_pairing_target_proof, never a server-side side channel and never an unsigned client claim.

public_key.description: Canonical PublicKey shape shared with agent-operations. For a staged device the key material is carried in `key` and `kid` is the target `ak:device:<uuid>` id.

device_pairing_state.description: Lifecycle state of a staged device-pairing short-link record. A staged record starts staged and account-less, moves one way to ready_for_claim once ak.gate.account.command.finalize_device_pairing.v1 attaches a valid target proof for an exact AccountId, flips to authorized once an authenticated device completes ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1, and reports expired once its bounded TTL has elapsed. There is no path back from ready_for_claim to staged and no path that reaches authorized without passing through ready_for_claim.

device_pairing_stage_request_body.description: Unauthenticated stage request that mints a fresh account-less pending pairing record. It carries only the canonical public key and a client nonce: the target proof cannot exist yet, because it must commit to the request id, pairing code, expiry, gate audience and server nonce that this call mints. It also deliberately omits hpke_key and algorithms; those reach the approving device inside the signed device_pairing_target_proof over the out-of-band channel, so the anonymous staging surface never accumulates long-term device key material or a device algorithm fingerprint. The record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it.

device_pairing_stage_outcome.description: Server-minted challenge inputs for the sole target proof. request id and pairing code are body-only anonymous lookup credentials; they MUST NOT enter URL path/query.

device_pairing_finalize_request_body.description: Authenticated one-way transition of a staged record from staged to ready_for_claim. The caller presents the exact request id and pairing code, holds the staged candidate key, and authenticates with the sender-constrained pending account handoff that supplies the exact AccountId. The service recomputes the device-lifecycle.md 2.1.2 challenge transcript from its own durable stage, verifies target_proof.device_signature with the staged new_device_pubkey, and requires target_proof.account_id to equal the AccountId bound to that handoff. Exact retry of the same intent returns the same outcome; the same request id with different content conflicts.

target_proof.description: The single signed target possession proof. This authenticated call is its only server-facing carrier; it is public, signature-protected material and carries no private key.

device_pairing_finalize_outcome.description: Result of attaching the target proof to a pending record. state is always ready_for_claim: the transition is one-way and the operation never reports a state it did not reach.

device_pairing_resolve_request_body.description: Body-only resolver input for device-pairing short-link handoff. The token is obtained from a URL fragment or equivalent out-of-band channel and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query.

device_pairing_bootstrap.description: Anonymous challenge inputs used to independently recompute the staged challenge digest before checking the out-of-band target proof. Contains no target proof, HPKE key or algorithm fingerprint. No authorization is granted.

device_pairing_code_claim_request_body.description: Authenticated claim of one pending pairing request by its normalized eight-character code. The caller is a current accepted, non-pending-revocation device of an exact AccountId and presents nothing else: the code is the whole input and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. Unknown, wrong, expired, cross-account, not yet finalized and already consumed codes MUST all return the same not_found.

device_pairing_code_claim_outcome.description: Everything the approving device needs to verify the claimed request locally: the same bootstrap the short-link resolve returns and the byte-equivalent signed target proof. It carries no private key, no session credential, no recovery material and nothing about any other device of the account. Claiming retrieves a request and grants nothing; an accepted device still has to sign ak.device.authorize.

target_proof.description: The exact proof attached at finalize. It MUST be byte-equivalent to the proof a QR or link carries for the same request; the code entry point MUST NOT produce a weaker code-only authorization branch.

device_pairing_status_request_body.description: Body-only poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found).

device_pairing_status_outcome.description: Authorization status for a staged device-pairing record. While the record is still account-less the state is staged; after finalize it is ready_for_claim. Once an authenticated device has authorized this pairing, state is authorized and device_id plus authorized_event_ref are present. An open record whose bounded TTL has elapsed reports state expired.

authorized_event_ref.description: Accepted ak.device.authorize Event id. It is the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check in crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.4.1: before the target device assembles the identity locally it MUST fetch this Event and confirm byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical device_public_key_did, hpke_key and algorithms, and an expected complete AccountId, or fail closed.

device_pairing_target_proof.description:
The single target possession proof for staged accepted_device pairing. Sign UTF8("ak.device_authorize_accepted_device_possession_proof.v1
") || JCS(all fields except device_signature). The unsigned challenge digest is independently recomputed from the server record; the signed descriptor covers the exact AccountId this pairing is being finalized against, the target key, the HPKE key, the algorithms and the binding kind. The candidate can only sign it after it has obtained that AccountId from its own sender-constrained pending account handoff, so this object exists from finalize on and never at stage time. It reaches the server exactly once, through the authenticated finalize call, and the anonymous stage and resolve request surfaces MUST NOT accept it. The approved Event retains the descriptor and the challenge digest so its signature stays re-verifiable after stage cleanup.

account_id.description: Complete AccountId this pairing request is bound to. A verifier MUST compare it byte-for-byte against the AccountId the finalizing pending account handoff is bound to, and the target device MUST compare it against the accepted Event actor_id.account_id before local assembly. A server-side field, a route, a session audience or an unsigned request body member MUST NOT substitute for it.

device_public_key_did.description: Self-describing did:key form of the same Ed25519 key as new_device_pubkey.key. A verifier MUST reject an proof whose device_public_key_did decodes to different key bytes than the staged or forwarded new_device_pubkey.

hpke_key.description: Target device X25519 HPKE public key. This proof is its authority; a service MUST NOT supply or substitute it.

authorization_binding_kind.description: This transcript exists only for accepted_device pairing. registration_anchor and pcr_recovery use their separate full possession objects, and a transcript from one binding kind MUST NOT be accepted for another.

pairing_challenge_transcript_digest.description: SHA-256 of the domain-separated canonical staged challenge bytes defined in device-lifecycle.md 2.1.2. Verifiers independently reconstruct it from bootstrap/server stage. Covers request id, code, audience, expiry, both nonces, staged key and metadata digest; never accepts a caller-self-reported challenge.

device_signature.description: Ed25519 signature by the private key of device_public_key_did over the canonical signing input above. The approving device MUST copy it byte-for-byte into device_authorize_payload.device_signature and into the pair_device request device_signature.
